instructions: Finely chop the onion until you have about 1/2 cup. Finely chop half the bell pepper. Chop 4 tbsp of the cilantro. Chop the green chilies and put them in a small bowl for the table.
Crack the 8 eggs into a large bowl and beat until frothy. Add the onion, bell pepper, cilantro, 1 tsp salt, the turmeric, the black pepper and the chaat masala. Beat again.
Spread the butter over one side of each of the 8 slices of bread.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Pour in a quarter of the egg mix, about 1/2 cup, and spread it to roughly the size of a slice of bread. Pour a second quarter beside it.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the bottoms are set. Flip each one and cook for 1 minute.
Fold the edges of each omelette in so it's a square that fits the bread. Transfer them to a plate.
Repeat with 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the egg mix to make 4 omelettes in all.
Wipe out the skillet and set it over medium heat with 1 tbsp of the oil. Put 2 slices of bread in the pan, buttered side up, and lay an omelette on each.
Top each with a second slice, buttered side down. Toast for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden, then flip and toast the other side for 1 to 2 minutes.
Repeat with the last 2 omelettes and the remaining oil.
Cut each sandwich in half. Serve hot with the ketchup and the chopped green chilies on the side.
method_notes: Swasthi's Recipes leads (5 stars from 57): beaten eggs with onion, capsicum, coriander, turmeric and pepper, cooked as a flat omelette and toasted between two slices of bread. Easy Indian Cookbook (also 5 from 57) folds the omelette to the size of the bread and adds chutney, and Honey, What's Cooking has only 1 rating. The cheese all three offer is left out, and the green chili goes on the side to keep the sandwich mild. Cooked two omelettes at a time in a large skillet, four sandwiches take about 25 minutes, not the 10 the single-sandwich versions show.
